attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. The X replies he quotes are other people's and are not graded.

semantics.note: Faithful. The claim is a present-tense observation, and 'anymore' (a decline) is kept. The business aside is rightly left out. 'Hardly anyone' is hyperbole with no threshold.

contract.note: The plain reading (only a very small share of the public trusts OpenAI) is the ordinary one. But no poll measures trust directly, so using favorability as a proxy and choosing which denominator to count is an interpretation the speaker did not supply. The result turns on it.

evidence.note: Pollster's own dashboard. National voter poll fielded May 2-4, 2026, in the period: OpenAI net favorability -41. This points to broad negativity, but the favorable share is not given, so the support condition (a small minority favorable, clear majorities against) is not shown.
Single-choice question on which company is most trusted to develop AI responsibly. It shows low relative trust, not the share of people who trust OpenAI at all. Weak proxy.

Secondary report of The Argument poll, fielded May 29-June 3, in the period: net +11 among the 87% who knew OpenAI. That implies a sizeable favorable share. The primary report is paywalled and the methods are undisclosed.
Change Research, March 2026, before the period: 12% favorable, 49% unfavorable. Context only. It shows how much results depend on wording and denominator.

reviews.rationale: The in-period polls conflict. Veleonis finds OpenAI deeply underwater (-41 net) but gives no favorable share. The Argument (via a secondary report) finds +11 net among those who know the company. Neither measures trust directly, and none dates from August, when the claim was made. The support condition is not met and the contradiction rests on one secondary, paywalled source that conflicts with a primary one, so the packet does not settle the outcome.
